blocks.content: The server-sent-events topic covered a genuinely useful, but strictly one directional channel. Websockets close that remaining gap entirely, providing a real, persistent connection where BOTH the client and the server can send messages to each other at any time, in either direction, completely independent of the traditional request and response pattern.

If you have ever used a live chat application, or played a real time multiplayer game in a browser, websockets were almost certainly the actual mechanism carrying that instant, back and forth communication.

1. The Key Difference From Server Sent Events
blocks.text: 1. The Key Difference From Server Sent Events

blocks.content: Server sent events, covered in the previous topic, is genuinely one directional, server to client only. Websockets remove that specific restriction entirely, providing a real, genuinely two way channel where either side, client or server, can send a message to the other at any moment, with neither side needing to wait for the other to ask first.
/engineering/library/cn/images/1785437870007-578599380.png
blocks.alt: The Key Difference From Server Sent Events

blocks.content: 2. How a Websocket Connection Actually Starts
blocks.text: 2. How a Websocket Connection Actually Starts

blocks.content: A websocket connection genuinely begins as an ordinary HTTP request, but this specific request includes a header asking to upgrade the connection to a websocket. If the server agrees, the connection switches protocols right there, from that point forward it is a genuine, persistent websocket connection, no longer behaving like ordinary HTTP at all.
/engineering/library/cn/images/1785437870007-311522828.png
blocks.alt: How a Websocket Connection Actually Starts

blocks.title: A genuinely clever bootstrap mechanism
blocks.content: Starting from an ordinary HTTP request lets websockets work smoothly through existing web infrastructure already built to understand HTTP, before switching over to its own genuinely different, persistent behavior once the upgrade is actually accepted.
3. One Persistent Connection, Many Messages

Once established, a websocket connection stays open, and both sides can exchange as many separate messages as they want over it, over time, with no need to repeat any handshake or connection setup between individual messages at all.
/engineering/library/cn/images/1785437870007-485128123.png
4. Why This Genuinely Means Lower Latency
blocks.text: 4. Why This Genuinely Means Lower Latency

blocks.content: Ordinary HTTP requests, even efficient ones, carry real header and connection overhead on every single exchange. Once a websocket connection is actually open, individual messages carry dramatically less overhead, since the expensive setup work only ever happens once, at the very start, not repeated for every single message afterward.

blocks.alt: Why This Genuinely Means Lower Latency

5. Real, Natural Use Cases

A live chat application, where messages need to appear instantly in both directions, is a natural fit. A real time multiplayer game, where player actions need to be reflected to everyone else almost instantly, fits just as well. Collaborative editing, where several people are genuinely editing the exact same document live at once, is another genuinely natural use case, needing frequent, low latency updates flowing both ways.
/engineering/library/cn/images/1785437870008-441297735.png

blocks.title: The common thread across all these use cases
blocks.content: Every one of these examples genuinely needs BOTH sides sending data frequently and with low latency, exactly the specific need websockets exists to serve well.
6. The Full Progression, Tied Together

This module has now covered a genuine, deliberate progression: polling repeats full requests, most finding nothing new. Long polling reduces that waste by having the server wait to respond. Server sent events eliminates repeated connection setup entirely, but only in one direction. Websockets close the final gap, one persistent connection, genuinely both directions.
/engineering/library/cn/images/1785437870009-871928106.png
7. Choosing the Right Tool

If an application genuinely needs both sides sending data frequently, in real time, websockets is the natural fit. If only the server ever actually needs to push updates, with the client never needing to send meaningful data back over that same channel, server sent events is simpler, and perfectly sufficient, no need to reach for the added complexity of websockets unnecessarily.

items: Reaching for websockets by default for every real time need, when server sent events is simpler and perfectly sufficient for genuinely one directional cases.
Assuming a websocket connection is somehow unrelated to HTTP, when it genuinely begins life as an ordinary HTTP request asking to upgrade.
Websockets provide one persistent, genuinely two way connection, unlike server sent events strictly one directional stream.
The expensive connection setup cost is paid once, keeping individual messages afterward lightweight and low latency.
Choosing between server sent events and websockets comes down to whether the client genuinely needs to send data back frequently too.
